newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mayors OK brownfield, water resolutions.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mayors OK brownfield, water resolutions.

text.p: U.S. mayors on Tuesday urged Congress to reauthorize landmark water cleanup legislation, to fund water infrastructure programs, and to set up a broad "brownfields" strategy.
The resolutions were adopted by the U.S. Conference of Mayors, holding its 65th annual conference in San Francisco.
Brownfields are pieces of lightly contaminated land in urban centers that do not qualify for Superfund toxic waste cleanup funding.
The conference voted Monday to urge Congress to adopt broad brownfields legislation giving cities tools they need to clean up and redevelop blighted sites.
The legislation should include tax incentives to stimulate private investment in cleanup efforts, including expanded use of tax-exempt bond financing, the resolution said.
The mayors called for continued funding of the Clean Water and Drinking Water State Revolving Funds at least at levels proposed by the Clinton Administration for the next five years.
In addition, the mayors said they supported the reauthorization of the Federal Clean Water Act.
